subject.title: [Bug]: Slack replies ~2s slower than other channels — dominant cost is Socket Mode event delivery; channel-side stalls fixed in #101888

question: Should Slack setup guidance make HTTP Request URLs the recommended production path for hosted deployments with public HTTPS ingress, while keeping Socket Mode as the local/private-network default?
rationale: The remaining dominant latency is upstream Socket Mode event delivery before OpenClaw runs, so changing docs/setup emphasis is a product and deployment-guidance decision rather than a narrow runtime bug fix.

options.title: Recommend HTTP for hosted production
options.body: Document and surface `mode: "http"` as the preferred low-latency Slack transport when public HTTPS ingress is available, while retaining Socket Mode for local and private deployments.

options.title: Add neutral tradeoff docs
options.body: Keep setup defaults unchanged and add a latency tradeoff note comparing Socket Mode and HTTP Request URLs.

options.title: Accept current guidance
options.body: Record that the current deployment-shape comparison is sufficient and close only after a maintainer explicitly accepts the Socket Mode latency limitation.

recommendation.title: Recommend HTTP for hosted production
recommendation.body: Document and surface `mode: "http"` as the preferred low-latency Slack transport when public HTTPS ingress is available, while retaining Socket Mode for local and private deployments.

likelyOwner.reason: They provided the latency decomposition, merged the related Slack runtime fixes, and left the clearest current scope for the HTTP guidance decision.
